correctness.rationale: Every joint degree-one event is counted by an induced matching on j specified vertices, with each unmatched one taking a neighbor outside and all edges on the complement free. Expanding products 1-2X_v gives all eigenvalues. Explicit exact small-order spectra through n=8 settle the exceptions; for n>=8 the strict union bound proves positivity, while conditional degree-one forcing proves strictly decreasing shell values for n>=9. The sharp conditioning follows from the exact n=4..8 minima and a uniform n>=9 estimate; the asymptotic follows from the bounded pair-degree-one probability and a pointwise second-factorial-moment remainder. verify.py independently checks graph histograms, Walsh transforms and the displayed integers (591 passed assertions). The all-n steps are inequalities in the proof, not claims of exhaustive experimental verification.

value.rationale: The random subset of vertices of degree exactly one is an intrinsic full-graph statistic with dependent coordinates. Its Boolean convolution operator is a natural information-loss and deconvolution object, and the entire spectrum, sharp all-dimensional conditioning, first singular orders and nonmonotone low-order least-frequency transition are not determined by the customary one-vertex binomial count alone. A structural forced-matching lemma and conditional signed-probability argument identify the all-order extremal frequency, with a quantitative inverse stability asymptotic; no downstream application is asserted as proved.
